works.title: The Oath of Enmity
works.source: Polybius, Histories · trans. E. S. Shuckburgh, 1889 · Project Gutenberg #44125 · public domain
works.note: Hannibal’s own account, given years later to King Antiochus, of the oath his father made him swear at age nine — never to be a friend to Rome.

works.title: The Appeal to Scipio, before Zama
works.source: Livy, History of Rome · Project Gutenberg #12582 · public domain
works.note: The speech Livy gives Hannibal at his parley with Scipio on the eve of Zama, 202 BCE — a plea for peace from the man who had ravaged Italy for sixteen years.

works.title: The Greatest Generals, at Ephesus
works.source: Livy, History of Rome · Project Gutenberg #12582 · public domain
works.note: The famous exchange: asked by Scipio to name the greatest commanders, Hannibal ranks Alexander, then Pyrrhus, then himself — with a barbed compliment for the man who beat him. As reported by Livy.

works.note: Polybius on the descent into Italy, 218 BCE — the snow, the precipices, and the landslip that halted the elephants.

works.note: Polybius on Hannibal’s masterpiece, 2 August 216 BCE: the double envelopment that annihilated a far larger Roman army — still studied as the perfect battle.
